primary_estimand: Contractile-activity-specific transcriptome response: exercised (Ex) vs contralateral non-exercised (NE) vastus lateralis at +1 h and +4 h after 60-min one-legged knee extension, within subject, in untrained and (after 2 mo aerobic training) trained state; secondary: training effect on baseline transcriptome (trained vs untrained baseline).
planned_contrasts: Ex vs NE at +1 h, untrained (abstract: 'DEGs between exercised and nonexercised muscle were evaluated at 1 and 4 h'; no count in abstract)
Ex vs NE at +4 h, untrained (same locator; no count in abstract)
Ex vs NE at +1 h, trained (GEO summary: 'in both untrained and trained skeletal muscle'; no count)
Ex vs NE at +4 h, trained (same; no count)
trained vs untrained at baseline (abstract: 'Transcriptome change at baseline after 2 mo of aerobic training'; no count)
inclusion: 7 untrained males, 84 samples = 7 subjects x 2 training states x 3 times x 2 legs (GEO overall design)
repeated_measure_unit: subject (all 12 conditions from each of 7 men)
normalization: DESeq normalization of HTSeq counts (GEO data_processing)
paper_method: DESeq family (GEO data_processing: HTSeq counts, 'Normalization of read counts provided by DESeq method'); exact DE model, pairing and threshold not stated in abstract

paper_threshold.source_locator: not in abstract; full text unavailable

paper_results: Abstract only: contractile-activity-specific responses were increases only (no decreased genes), regulated by CREB/ATF/AP1, MYC/MAX, E2F TFs; training-induced baseline changes (up and down) were more pronounced than acute contractile-specific responses and involved IRF/STAT TFs. GEO summary: contractile-specific responses in trained muscle substantially decreased relative to untrained.
